content.overview: Establishment joins donor biology, explant selection and aseptic execution. Contamination timing and distribution are investigation clues, not automatic proof of a source or operator failure.

vocabulary.definition: Plant tissue introduced into an in-vitro culture system.
The distribution of affected vessels across time, source material, batches and process steps.

sections.title: Starting material shapes establishment
sections.body: Donor condition, explant type, developmental position and genotype can change survival and response. These variables should be recorded rather than hidden inside a single success rate.

sections.title: Timing helps rank hypotheses
sections.body: Early widespread growth may point toward preparation or workflow exposure, while clustered or delayed findings may support different hypotheses. Timing narrows investigation but does not identify an organism by itself.

sections.title: Triage protects evidence and adjacent work
sections.body: Affected material should follow defined isolation and disposition rules. Images, vessel IDs, batch links and event timing should be preserved before cleanup removes useful evidence.

workedExamples: Contamination across different genotypes that shared one preparation lot makes that common factor worth testing without proving it was the source.
Low survival confined to one explant type can be biological or procedural; compare condition and handling records before changing the entire protocol.
commonMistakes: Discarding affected vessels before recording the pattern.
Changing donor, medium and workflow at the same time.
content.practicalApplication: Triage a mock vessel log, separate contamination from noncontamination establishment failures, rank three hypotheses and specify the next discriminating check for each.
content.summary: Establishment troubleshooting uses source, explant, vessel, timing and workflow evidence to localize failure while protecting unaffected work.
